items.title: The mod-two square algebra, admissible sequences, and excess
items.statement:
Assume AC, inherited from the cited bundle, cohomology, or operation suppliers. Let $T=\mathbb F_2\langle s_1,s_2,\ldots\rangle$ be the vector space with basis the finite words in the symbols $s_j$ for $j>0$, including the empty word, and with multiplication the bilinear extension of concatenation. Concatenation is associative and the empty word is its unit, so this explicitly constructs the free associative graded algebra, with $|s_j|=j$ and $s_0=1$. Define $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{Adem}}$ as its quotient by the two-sided ideal generated by

$$s_a s_b+\sum_{j=0}^{\lfloor a/2\rfloor} \binom{b-j-1}{a-2j}s_{a+b-j}s_j, \qquad 0<a<2b.$$

A normalized sequence $I=(i_1,\ldots,i_k)$ has positive entries; the empty sequence denotes the unit. It is admissible if $i_j\ge 2i_{j+1}$. Write $|I|=\sum_j i_j$, put $i_{k+1}=0$, and define

$$d_j(I)=i_j-2i_{j+1},\qquad e(I)=\sum_{j=1}^k d_j(I)=i_1-i_2-\cdots-i_k.$$

For the empty sequence set $|I|=e(I)=0$. The square algebra $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{Sq}}$ is the image of the free algebra under $s_j\mapsto Sq^j$ in natural mod-two cohomology operations, allowing every nonnegative input degree. The published Adem theorem makes the induced map $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{Adem}}\to\mathcal A_{\mathrm{Sq}}$ well defined. The admissible-composites theorem proves it is an isomorphism.

Every relation is homogeneous. A quotient by a two-sided ideal is a unital associative graded algebra: products of cosets are independent of representatives since multiplying an ideal element on either side remains in the ideal. Its grading is the direct sum of homogeneous quotient spaces since the generating relations are homogeneous. The displayed finite sums defining degree and excess are unambiguous; admissibility makes each $d_j$ nonnegative. Composition and addition of the published natural linear operations preserve naturality, so the image algebra exists. Each square commutes with suspension by the published normalization/suspension proposition, so the resulting composites are stable wherever their source degrees are defined. No assertion that *every* stable operation is such a composite is needed for this definition.
items.strategy: Construct the free associative word algebra by concatenation, then take its quotient by the homogeneous two-sided Adem ideal. Verify representative independence, associativity, the unit and quotient grading directly. Define degree, admissibility and excess by finite sums, including the empty word; the nonnegative admissibility differences telescope to excess. The published Adem relations give the quotient-to-square-operation map. Naturality, linearity, composition and the published suspension identity give its stable image algebra. Spanning, independence and the presentation are proved by Items 2–4; no classification of all stable operations is assumed.

items.title: Local path-fibration and cohomology inputs for mod-two Eilenberg–Mac Lane induction
items.statement: Assume AC. For $q\ge2$, $K_q$ is simply connected, $\widetilde H^j(K_q;\mathbb F_2)=0$ for $j<q$, and $H^q(K_q;\mathbb F_2)=\mathbb F_2\iota_q$. The actual contractible mapping-path fibration has strict loop fiber $F=\Omega K_q$. There is a marked weak equivalence $h:K_{q-1}\to F$ inducing an isomorphism of mod-two cohomology rings $h^*:H^*(F;\mathbb F_2)\xrightarrow{\cong}H^*(K_{q-1};\mathbb F_2)$. Its natural multiplicative cohomological Serre spectral sequence has constant fiber system. No claim that $F$ has CW homotopy type or that $h$ is a homotopy equivalence is needed. In particular its abutment vanishes in positive degrees.
items.strategy: Use ordinary Hurewicz and cohomology UCT on the CW base to obtain its lower vanishing and normalized first class. Apply direct mapping-path factorization to the marked basepoint inclusion; the actual total contracts, and the fibration LES computes the connected strict loop fiber's marking and homotopy groups. Extend its basepoint by a weak CW approximation, identify that CW model with the marked K(F_2,q-1) by uniqueness, and adjust the uniqueness map to be based via the CW-point cofibration and moving-basepoint formula. Their composite is a marked weak equivalence. The published weak-equivalence homology lemma, natural coefficient UCT and field duality make its cohomology map an isomorphism; cup naturality makes it a ring isomorphism. Apply the multiplicative Serre theorem to the actual fibration with trivial monodromy. No strict-fiber CW-type theorem is imported.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
references.locator: Section 4.2, printed pp. 376–377: the path-space fibration; Section 4.1, Proposition 4.13: CW approximation. The required strict-fiber cohomology comparison is proved locally via the published weak-equivalence homology and coefficient interfaces.

items.title: Infinite real projective space is a marked mod-two Eilenberg–Mac Lane space
items.statement: Assume AC. Infinite real projective space, with the marking of its fundamental group given by the nontrivial antipodal deck transformation, is a CW $K(\mathbb F_2,1)$. Its degree-one ring generator is its normalized mod-two fundamental class, so its cohomology is $\mathbb F_2[\iota_1]$.
items.strategy: Identify the stable sphere and rank-one Grassmannian models. Coordinate-positive unit representatives give local sections of the antipodal double cover; their finite-stage formulas are continuous in the weak topologies. The covering homotopy-lifting theorem makes it a fibration, and stable Stiefel contractibility gives no higher base homotopy. Endpoint deck transformations identify the fundamental group with Z/2, with injectivity from a contraction of a closed lifted loop and surjectivity from a path joining antipodes. Schubert cells give the CW structure. The published polynomial projective-space cohomology ring has a unique nonzero degree-one class, which is therefore the normalized fundamental class. Marked uniqueness transfers it to the chosen CW model.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Vector Bundles & K-Theory
references.locator: Section 1.2, printed pp. 28–31: stable sphere, Grassmannian and universal bundle models.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology

items.title: Steenrod squares commute with relative cohomology connectors
items.statement: For every pair $(E,F)$, the mod-two cohomology connector satisfies $\delta Sq^a(x)=Sq^a\delta(x)$ for every $x\in H^m(F;\mathbb F_2)$ and every nonnegative $a$. Relative squares use the published relative cup-$i$ construction.
items.strategy: Extend a fiber cocycle u by zero to a cochain b on the ambient space and put c=db, a relative representative of the connector. For 0≤a≤m set j=m-a. The cochain b cup_(j+1) db + b cup_j b restricts to a representative of Sq^a[u], and the published cup-i coboundary identity makes its coboundary c cup_(j+1) c, representing Sq^a[c]. At a=m+1 use the relative primitive b cup_0 db; larger operations vanish by instability. The relative carrier property and characteristic two justify all cancellations and relative representatives, including degree-zero inputs.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 1
references.locator: Lemma 1.35, printed p. 55: compatibility of squares with cohomological transgression; connector compatibility is proved cochain-wise in the local draft.

items.title: Fiber and limit isomorphisms force a base-axis isomorphism
items.statement:
Let $\Phi:\bar E\to E$ be a morphism of first-quadrant cohomological spectral sequences of vector spaces, with $d_r$ of bidegree $(r,1-r)$ and

$$\bar E_2^{p,q}=\bar E_2^{p,0}\otimes\bar E_2^{0,q},\qquad E_2^{p,q}=E_2^{p,0}\otimes E_2^{0,q}.$$

Assume $\Phi_2$ factors as the tensor product of its axis maps, the fiber-axis map is an isomorphism, and $\Phi_\infty$ is an isomorphism in every position. Then the base-axis map $\Phi_2^{p,0}$ is an isomorphism in every degree.
items.strategy: Induct on the base column k. The tensor factorization and fiber-axis isomorphism give E_2 isomorphisms through that column. Induction on r yields page-r isomorphisms in columns p≤k-r+1 and injections in columns p≤k, by comparing cycles and incoming boundaries. At the next bottom position (k+1,0), compare the incoming-differential exact sequences. For each incoming source, use finite downward induction from its stationary limit to prove surjectivity on its cycle subgroup; later outgoing differentials have negative fiber target. Starting from the limiting bottom isomorphism, descend in r using this cycle surjectivity and the other exact-sequence isomorphisms. This proves the next E_2 base-column isomorphism and closes the induction.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 1
references.locator: Theorem 1.36 and proof, printed pp. 56–58: fiber-axis and limiting isomorphisms imply the base-axis isomorphism.

items.title: A connected graded module coalgebra with injective unit orbit is free
items.statement: Assume AC and fix a field $k$. Let $A=\bigoplus_{i\ge0}A_i$ be a unital associative graded $k$-algebra with $A_0=k1_A$, equipped with a degree-preserving coassociative counital coproduct $\Delta_A$ such that $\Delta_A(1_A)=1_A\otimes1_A$ and $\Delta_A,\varepsilon_A$ are algebra homomorphisms for the Koszul multiplication $(a\otimes b)(c\otimes d)=(-1)^{|b||c|}ac\otimes bd$. Let $M=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}M_j$ be a coaugmented coassociative counital graded $k$-coalgebra with $M_0=ku$, $\varepsilon_M(u)=1$, and $\Delta_M(u)=u\otimes u$. Supply a $k$-bilinear unital left $A$-action satisfying $(ab)m=a(bm)$, $(\lambda1_A)m=\lambda m$, and $A_iM_j\subseteq M_{i+j}$. Give $M\otimes M$ the diagonal action $a(v\otimes w)=\sum(-1)^{|a_2||v|}(a_1v)\otimes(a_2w)$ for $\Delta_Aa=\sum a_1\otimes a_2$, and assume $\Delta_M(am)=a\Delta_M(m)$. If $\nu:A\to M$, $a\mapsto au$, is injective, set $A^+=\bigoplus_{i>0}A_i$ and $Q=M/A^+M$. Then $Q$ is nonnegatively graded with $Q_0=k\pi(u)$, and every graded $k$-linear section $f:Q\to M$ of $\pi$ induces a graded left $A$-module isomorphism $\Phi:A\otimes_kQ\to M$, $a\otimes q\mapsto af(q)$, with $A$ acting on the first tensor factor. Such a section exists under AC. Any homogeneous $k$-basis of $Q$ lifts under $f$ to a homogeneous free $A$-basis of $M$. No commutativity, antipode, or finite-type hypothesis is imposed; supplying the homogeneous basis and lifts removes additional choice from the proof.
items.strategy: Use the stated grading/action axioms as local definitions; no later graded-algebra page is needed. The Koszul tensor formula is well defined by tensor universality, and its associativity follows by comparing the signs $|b_2||v|+|a_2|(|b_1|+|v|)$ and $|a_2||b_1|+(|a_2|+|b_2|)|v|$. Grading and the counits give $\Delta_M(m)=u\otimes m+m\otimes u+$ lower bidegrees for positive-degree $m$, while degree zero has the single term $\Delta_M(\lambda u)=\lambda u\otimes u$. The graded submodule $A^+M$ has no degree-zero part, and $\pi(am)=\varepsilon_A(a)\pi(m)$. Choose degree-preserving lifts of homogeneous bases to construct $f$. Prove surjectivity of $\Phi$ by degree induction: $m-f\pi(m)$ is a finite sum of positive-degree $A$-multiples of lower-degree vectors. For injectivity put $T=(\mathrm{id}\otimes\pi)\Delta_M$. Compatibility and the counit show $T(am)=aT(m)$ because terms with positive-degree second coproduct factor are killed by $\pi$. For homogeneous $q$ of degree $d$, $T\Phi(a\otimes q)=\nu(a)\otimes q+$ terms of second degree less than $d$, including the separate $d=0$ case. Write a putative kernel vector as a finite sum $\sum a_j\otimes q_j$ in a homogeneous basis of $Q$ and select its largest second degree. Projection there and the coordinate functionals force $\nu(a_j)=0$, hence $a_j=0$, a contradiction. Tensor/direct-sum and unit isomorphisms identify $A\otimes Q$ with a direct sum of copies of the potentially noncommutative ring $A$, yielding the claimed free basis.

references.title: Tom Weston, An Introduction to Cobordism Theory
references.locator: Section 6, Lemma 6.1 and Proposition 6.2 with complete proof, printed pp.11–13; homogeneous-section and degree-zero corrections are proved locally.

items.title: Finite-cover transfer with inverted degree and sign anti-invariants
items.statement: Assume AC. Let p:Y→X be a nonempty finite d-sheeted regular cover of path-connected CW spaces, and let R be a commutative unital ring in which d is invertible. Pullback identifies H*(X;R) with the deck-invariant graded subalgebra H*(Y;R)^G. For a double cover and 2 invertible, let O_R be its associated sign local system. Then H*(X;O_R) is naturally the anti-invariant part of H*(Y;R). No finite-dimensionality hypothesis is imposed.
items.strategy: Sum all lifts of each singular simplex to obtain the integral chain transfer τ; face restriction bijects lift sets, so τ commutes with boundary. On R-valued cochains the identities Tp*=d·id and p*T=Σg* prove injectivity and the invariant-image assertion. Identify sign-local-system cochains with anti-invariant cochains upstairs by signed lift coordinates and face transport. The cochain idempotents (1±σ*)/2 split the complex and therefore split cohomology. Ring identification comes from pullback multiplicativity, not transfer multiplicativity.

references.title: Tom Weston, An Introduction to Cobordism Theory
references.locator: §17, Corollary 17.2; sign-cochain and general inverted-degree extensions proved locally

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
references.locator: §3.G, Transfer Homomorphisms, printed pp.321–326

items.title: Integral homology comparison gives finite-range homotopy comparison for simply connected CW complexes
items.statement: Assume AC. Let N≥2 and let f:(X,x₀)→(Y,y₀) be a based continuous map between nonempty path-connected simply connected CW complexes. Suppose f_*:H_i(X;Z)→H_i(Y;Z) is an isomorphism for 0≤i<N and a surjection for i=N. Then f_*:π_i(X,x₀)→π_i(Y,y₀) is an isomorphism for 1≤i<N and a surjection for i=N. No conclusion about π_{N+1} or homotopy equivalence of the spaces is included.
items.strategy: Replace f by a cellular map using cellular approximation and transfer based group statements through the homotopy track. Form its genuine CW mapping cylinder M with source subcomplex X and target deformation retraction. The relative homology exact sequence forces H_i(M,X;Z)=0 through N. Simple connectivity gives relative π₁=*. Induct on m=2,…,N: lower relative homotopy vanishing makes the CW pair (m−1)-connected, and relative Hurewicz identifies π_m(M,X) with the zero H_m(M,X). The relative homotopy exact sequence gives isomorphisms on π_i below N and surjectivity at N. Retract to Y and undo basepoint transport.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Chapter 4
references.locator: Theorem 4.32 and Corollary 4.33, printed pp.366–368; finite-range endpoint proved locally

items.title: Rationalization is exact and commutes with singular homology
items.statement: Assume AC. For every abelian group A, A⊗_Z Q is its positive-integer localization: every element is a/s and a/s=0 iff a is killed by some positive integer. Thus A⊗Q=0 iff A is torsion. Rationalization is exact and commutes with direct sums. Naturally for every space Y, H_j(Y;Z)⊗Q≅H_j(Y;Q); for every rational vector space V, H_j(Y;V)≅H_j(Y;Q)⊗_Q V.
items.strategy: Apply exact module localization and its tensor identification to the cycle/boundary short exact sequences of the singular chain complex. Clear denominators to obtain the torsion criterion. A basis of V identifies tensoring a rational complex with V with a direct sum; finite-support coordinate kernels and images give the natural coefficient comparison.

references.title: Altman and Kleiman, A Term of Commutative Algebra, 13th edition
references.locator: Corollary 12.13, Theorem 12.20, and Corollary 12.22: tensor description, exactness, and sums/quotients of localization

items.title: Weak-join classifying model of a discrete group
items.statement:
For a discrete group G, let J(G) be the weak geometric realization of the abstract simplicial complex with vertices (s,g), s∈N and g∈G, whose nonempty simplices contain at most one vertex in each slot s; include the empty simplex. Right multiplication on every label defines a G-action. Define B_wG=J(G)/G with the orbit quotient topology. Its geometric realization uses the published simplex-wise weak topology, not an alternative Milnor-model topology.

The construction is unambiguous: the vertex set and the simplex condition are defined by comprehension, and right multiplication $(s,h)\cdot g=(s,hg)$ preserves slot distinctness, so it is an automorphism of the abstract simplicial complex and restricts to a homeomorphism of the geometric realization. The orbit quotient and its quotient topology are therefore well defined as an ordinary quotient space, and the quotient map is continuous by definition of the quotient topology. The definition selects nothing; orbit representatives are needed only in later arguments and are handled there. The weak (simplex-wise) topology is the one fixed by [[def-geometric-realization-of-an-abstract-simplicial-complex]], not an alternative join-model topology.
items.strategy: Define the downward-closed simplex family and its published weak realization; label translation preserves slots and faces, so gives a continuous action, with the CW and covering properties justified in the following lemma.

references.title: John Milnor, Construction of Universal Bundles II
references.locator: Sections 2–3 and 5, printed pp.430–433 and 435–436; join construction and weak CW variant, specialized and justified for discrete groups in local rows 2–3

items.title: Oriented Grassmannians have two lifted Schubert cells
items.statement: Assume AC, inherited from the cited bundle, cohomology, or operation suppliers. For n≥1, the forgetful map Gr⁺_n(R∞)=BSO(n)→Gr_n(R∞)=BO(n) is a two-sheeted cover, including n=1, where it is S∞→RP∞. Each Schubert cell has exactly two lifted cells, and these cells give BSO(n) the CW weak topology with finite boundary support. Set BSO(0) to the point.
items.strategy: Use oriented orthonormal-frame charts to exhibit the two local sheets; lift each contractible Schubert characteristic disk to both sheets. Finite skeleta are compact Hausdorff finite attaching quotients. Check the infinite closed-set topology against the base weak-topology test on evenly covered charts, proving the lifted cells give precisely the CW weak topology.

references.title: John Milnor and James Stasheff, Characteristic Classes
references.locator: Chapters 16–17, universal Thom and oriented Grassmannian constructions; the two-sheeted cover and lifted weak-topology argument is proved locally.

items.title: Adem reduction spans by admissible square composites
items.statement: Assume AC, inherited from the cited bundle, cohomology, or operation suppliers. In degree $N\ge0$, every element of $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{Adem}}$ is a finite linear combination of the admissible words $s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_k}$ with $|I|=N$. Consequently the same is true in $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{Sq}}$.
items.strategy: In degree N pad normalized positive sequences with terminal zeros to length N and order the finite set lexicographically. Each Adem replacement of a nonadmissible adjacent pair (a,b) replaces it by (a+b-j,j) with j<b, so its first changed entry strictly increases. Removing a terminal identity after that entry preserves the increase. Descending induction on this finite order terminates in admissible words, preserving total degree. The unit handles degree zero. Pass through the quotient-to-operation map to obtain the operation spanning assertion without assuming independence.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
references.locator: Section 4.L, printed p. 499: lexicographic Adem reduction.

items.title: Admissible square actions have distinct leading monomials
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $I=(i_1,\ldots,i_k)$ be admissible, let $r\ge e(I)$, and choose $L\ge |I|+1$. On

$$X=(\mathbb{RP}^{L})^r, \qquad H^*(X;\mathbb F_2)= \mathbb F_2[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_1^{L+1},\ldots,x_r^{L+1}),$$

put $P=x_1\cdots x_r$. Order monomials lexicographically by their exponent vectors, largest first. The largest monomial of $Sq^I(P)$ has coefficient one and has exponents

$$(\underbrace{2^k,\ldots,2^k}_{d_k}, \underbrace{2^{k-1},\ldots,2^{k-1}}_{d_{k-1}}, \ldots, \underbrace{2,\ldots,2}_{d_1}, \underbrace{1,\ldots,1}_{r-e(I)}).$$

For fixed total degree $|I|$, different admissible sequences have different largest monomials. The empty sequence gives $P$.
items.strategy: Compute finite projective-space cohomology and its product ring using the published cellular and finite-free Künneth interfaces. Cartan and the top-square identity give Sq^a(x^m)=binom(m,a)x^(m+a); for m a power of two the only possible actions are no change or doubling. Regard each composite as a finite schedule of doublings. For a sequence of length k, at most i_k variables can reach exponent 2^k; reaching that maximum forces their complete doubling chains. Subtract their forced costs from the earlier budgets and induct on the residual admissible sequence. This proves both maximality and coefficient one, with multiplicities d_k,…,d_1. The exponent bound 1+|I| prevents truncation; backward recursion recovers I from these multiplicities. Distinct leading terms, rather than disjoint supports, prove the asserted distinction.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
references.locator: Section 4.L, printed pp. 490–491: square action on projective-space powers.

references.title: Tom Weston, An Introduction to Cobordism Theory
references.locator: Lemma 12.2, printed p. 23: the projective-product evaluation test. Its disjoint-support assertion is replaced by the local leading-monomial proof in the source draft.

items.title: The fundamental path-fibration class has the normalized relative lift
items.statement:
Assume AC. For $n\ge1$, in the marked path fibration $F=\Omega K_{n+1}\to P K_{n+1}\xrightarrow p K_{n+1}$, with the fiber identified in marked homology and cohomology with $K_n$ by the weak equivalence of Item 6,

\[
 \delta\iota_n=p^*\iota_{n+1}
 \quad\text{in }H^{n+1}(P K_{n+1},F;\mathbb F_2).
\]
items.strategy: Represent the marked nonzero fiber homotopy class by a based sphere map. Its Hurewicz image is the nonzero integral homology generator: transfer ordinary CW Hurewicz through Item 6's weak equivalence for n>1, and use abelianization for n=1. Nullhomotope the sphere in the contractible path space to a disk lift A. Its finite disk fundamental chain defines a relative generator z, whose pair-LES boundary is the marked fiber generator. The collapsed projected disk represents the marked base homotopy class by the fibration connecting map. The good-pair quotient and natural cellular comparison identify p_*z with its base Hurewicz image. Verify the relative, base and fiber UCT Ext terms vanish, explicitly using connected H_0 for n=1. Both the connector and pulled-back fundamental class evaluate as one on z, so relative evaluation UCT identifies them. No relative Hurewicz theorem or fiber homotopy-equivalence premise is used.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 1
references.locator: Proof of Theorem 1.32, printed p. 55: the fundamental path-fibration transgression. Generator and UCT normalizations are proved locally using absolute Hurewicz and the pair long exact sequences.

items.title: Relative lifts produce cohomological transgressions
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $p:E\to B$ be a Serre fibration over a simply connected CW base with basepoint vertex and fiber $F$. If $x\in H^m(F;\mathbb F_2)$, $m>0$, and $y\in H^{m+1}(B,*;\mathbb F_2)$ satisfy

\[
 \delta x=p^*y\quad\text{in }H^{m+1}(E,F;\mathbb F_2),
\]

then $x$ survives to $E_{m+1}^{0,m}$ and its differential $d_{m+1}$ is the bottom-axis coset represented by $y$. Moreover $Sq^a x$ has the same property with representative $Sq^a y$ at page $m+a+1$, whenever its degree is positive.
items.strategy: Lift the base class y to cohomology relative to the m-skeleton, using cellular vanishing and the pair LES. Choose its cocycle v vanishing on that skeleton. Extend a representative of x to E and correct it by a cochain vanishing on F so that its coboundary is exactly p^*v. This lies in skeletal filtration m+1, giving survival to that page and the specified bottom-axis coset differential by the filtered page formulas and Serre base-edge construction. Connector compatibility and relative square naturality give the analogous relative lift for Sq^a x; repeat the same argument in its new total degree. No unproved operation on spectral-sequence pages is assumed.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 1
references.locator: Lemma 1.35, printed p. 55, and the relative construction underlying Proposition 1.13, printed pp. 21–22: relative lifts and transgression.

items.title: Finite type and odd-primary acyclicity of K(F₂,q)
items.statement: Assume AC. For every q≥1 and every CW model K_q=K(Z/2,q), H_n(K_q;Z) is finitely generated for every n; for n>0 it is a finite 2-primary group. For every field F of characteristic different from two, H_n(K_q;F)=H^n(K_q;F)=0 for n>0 and H_0=H^0=F. The F₂ homology and cohomology are finite-dimensional degreewise, with H^i=0 for 0<i<q and H^q=F₂ with its normalized fundamental class. Positive integral cohomology is finite 2-primary. These are homological finite-type assertions, not finite-cell claims about arbitrary CW models.
items.strategy: Use the marked RP∞ model and its one-cell-per-degree Schubert structure for q=1; transfer from its contractible antipodal cover gives away-from-two field acyclicity. Induct via the actual contractible path fibration over K_q, comparing its strict loop fiber to K_{q−1} by weak CW approximation, marked EM uniqueness and weak-map homology invariance. In the integral homological Serre sequence, prove finite generation of the bottom-row group H_s(K_q;Z) by induction on s: it has no incoming differential, all finitely many outgoing targets are subquotients of lower-base-degree coefficient homology and are finitely generated by UCT and Noetherianity, and its terminal kernel is zero. For fields away from two the fiber has only H_0, so the contractible abutment forces base acyclicity. UCT and finite abelian-group decomposition then give finite 2-primary homology and the remaining coefficient assertions.

references.title: Tom Weston, An Introduction to Cobordism Theory
references.locator: §13, integral-versus-field comparison; reverse finite-generation induction proved locally

references.title: Charles Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 3
references.locator: §3.6, universal coefficient theorems

items.title: Finite-range comparison with an arbitrary simply connected target
items.statement: Assume AC. Let N≥2, X be a nonempty path-connected simply connected CW complex, Y an arbitrary nonempty path-connected simply connected space, and f:(X,x₀)→(Y,y₀) a based continuous map. If its integral homology maps are isomorphisms for 0≤i<N and surjective at N, its based homotopy maps are isomorphisms for 1≤i<N and surjective at N. No CW-type or ordinary product-CW hypothesis is required on Y.
items.strategy: Apply the relative construction of CW approximation directly to f:X→Y. It supplies a CW complex Z containing X as a subcomplex and a weak equivalence Q:Z→Y extending f literally. Its component and homotopy isomorphisms make Z path-connected and simply connected; weak-map integral homology invariance gives homology isomorphisms for Q. Therefore the inclusion j:X→Z inherits f’s precise homology hypotheses from Q_*j_*=f_*. Apply the CW comparison theorem to j and compose with Q_* on based homotopy groups. No lift through an unrelated CW approximation is claimed.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Chapter 4
references.locator: Proposition 4.13 and Theorem 4.32/Corollary 4.33; source-preserving CW extension uses the local published approximation construction

items.title: Rational cohomology of K(Z,n) through weak CW fiber comparison
items.statement: Assume AC. For each marked CW K(Z,n), n≥1, rational cohomology is Q[x_n] when n is even and Λ_Q(x_n) when n is odd, with |x_n|=n and x_n dual to the marked generator. In particular positive rational homology below 2n vanishes except for the one-dimensional group in degree n.
items.strategy: Weakly approximate the strict loop fiber and identify that CW approximation with the marked K(Z,n−1); the actual weak-equivalence map gives a rational cohomology ring isomorphism by homology comparison and field duality. Start with S^1. In the multiplicative path-fibration Serre sequence, an exterior fiber generator transgresses to x and multiplication by x is bijective in the necessary degrees, giving the even polynomial case. For the odd case the polynomial fiber generator has d_n(y^k)=k y^{k−1}x and x²=0; a hypothetical least extra base-degree class has no possible incoming differential after this page and would survive to the zero abutment. Field duality yields the asserted homology.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
references.locator: §5.1, cohomology spectral sequences and multiplicative structure, printed pp.543–549; strict-loop weak-CW comparison proved locally

items.title: The weak-join model is a CW K(G,1)
items.statement: Assume AC. For every discrete group G, J(G) and B_wG are CW complexes; J(G) is path-connected and weakly contractible, and J(G)→B_wG is a covering with fiber G. Therefore B_wG is a marked K(G,1), with the marking that sends a loop whose lift from the vertex $(0,1_G)$ ends at $(0,g)$ to $g^{-1}$, using left-to-right loop concatenation. For H≤G, B_wH embeds as a CW subcomplex of B_wG. Every finite set of cells of B_wG lies in B_wH for a finitely generated subgroup H≤G.
items.strategy: Attach simplex disks and orbit simplex disks with finite face support and use quotient map-out tests for the weak topology. On t_s>0 normalize the slot label to 1 to obtain explicit discrete covering charts. A compact sphere map has finite cell support; cone its image to a vertex in a fresh slot, then use basepoint transport to deduce based nullhomotopy. Apply the covering homotopy sequence. Normalize finitely many orbit simplices to first label 1 and generate H from the remaining labels.

items.title: Cohomology of BO and BSO away from two
items.statement: Assume AC. Let R be a nonzero commutative unital ring with 2 invertible. For m≥1, H*(BSO(2m+1);R)=R[p₁,…,p_m], H*(BSO(2m);R)=R[p₁,…,p_{m−1},e] with p_m=e², and H*(BO(2m);R)=H*(BO(2m+1);R)=R[p₁,…,p_m]. The indicated generators are the actual universal Euler and Pontryagin classes, |e|=2m and |p_i|=4i. Orientation reversal fixes p_i and negates e. BSO(1) has cohomology R in degree zero only, BO(1) likewise, and rank zero is a point. The chosen BSO(r) is the lifted Schubert CW model.
items.strategy: Use the separately justified two-lift Schubert CW structure and the actual universal oriented sphere bundle whose complement map has target BSO(n−1). Induct on n. At n=2m, Pontryagin generator lifts make restriction surjective in every degree; the degree-k Gysin sequence makes integration zero and multiplication by e injective on degree k−2m+1, with restriction kernel eH^{k−2m}. Degree induction gives generation, and repeated restriction followed by cancellation of e gives polynomial independence. The top-Pontryagin identity gives p_m=e². At odd rank the two-torsion Euler class vanishes over R, so restriction is injective. The sphere-vector involution reverses the even-dimensional complement orientation, forcing its image into the even Euler powers, already attained by the Pontryagin generators. Transfer identifies BO cohomology with the orientation-cover invariants.

items.title: Integral finite generation of universal real and oriented Thom homology
items.statement: Assume AC. For every r≥0 and every i≥0, H_i(MO(r);Z) and H_i(MSO(r);Z) are finitely generated. For positive rank the locally constructed homological Thom comparison is H_i(D(γ_r),S(γ_r);Z)=H_{i−r}(BO(r);O_Z(γ_r)), and likewise for γ_r⁺ with the constant orientation system. The disk/sphere quotient identifies these groups with reduced Thom homology. At rank zero the based quotient is B₊; BO(0)=BSO(0)=* gives S⁰ and is handled separately.
items.strategy: Filter the actual relative singular chains by F_p=(C_*(D_p)+C_*(S))/C_*(S). Orthogonalize trivializations over each characteristic disk continuously by Gram–Schmidt. For each finite Schubert skeleton the bundle is the compact product-disk attachment. Compare the graded chain-sum quotient with chains relative to D_{p−1}∪S_p using explicit sphere-preserving base collars, fiber collars, the two-open small-chain Mayer–Vietoris sequence and its homology equivalence. The good-pair quotient is a finite wedge of product-ball spheres, so the initial page has only the fiber-orientation row r. Its connector gives the cellular group-ring incidence Σ_g n_feg ε(g), retaining each incidence path’s orientation transport separately. Exact-couple stabilization and finite projected support of each cycle and primitive prove convergence and the homological Thom comparison. The base has finitely many Schubert cells in each degree (two lifted cells for BSO); finite free local cellular chains and Noetherianity give finite generation. Use the radial good-pair quotient only at positive rank.

items.title: The Thom prespectrum of the universal real and oriented bundles
items.statement: Assume AC, as inherited from the published bundle-classification suppliers. Let $\gamma_r\to B\mathrm O(r)$ and $\gamma_r^{+}\to B\mathrm{SO}(r)$ be the universal metric rank-$r$ bundles in the published Grassmannian models. For $r\ge0$ set $M\mathrm O_r=\mathrm{Th}(\gamma_r)$ and $M\mathrm{SO}_r=\mathrm{Th}(\gamma_r^{+})$, with the based rank-zero convention of the published Thom-space definition. Let $J(x_1,x_2,\ldots)=(0,x_1,x_2,\ldots)$. Fix $\iota_r(W)=\mathbb R e_1\oplus J(W)$ and its oriented version $(W,o)\mapsto(\mathbb R e_1\oplus J(W),e_1\wedge J_*o)$, the Grassmannian stabilization $\iota_r$ which adds the specified trivial coordinate line, with its fiberwise isometric identification $\varepsilon^1\oplus\gamma_r\cong\iota_r^*\gamma_{r+1}$; use $\varepsilon^1_+\oplus\gamma_r^+$ in the same first-coordinate order for its orientation-preserving counterpart. Define the structure map by the composite $S^1\wedge M\mathrm O_r\cong\mathrm{Th}(\varepsilon^1\oplus\gamma_r)\cong\mathrm{Th}(\iota_r^*\gamma_{r+1})\longrightarrow\mathrm{Th}(\gamma_{r+1})=M\mathrm O_{r+1}$, where the final arrow is induced by the pullback bundle projection covering $\iota_r$; the sphere coordinate is placed first as in the published prespectrum convention. The analogous maps define $M\mathrm{SO}$. Write $T_r=M\mathrm O_r$, $T_r^+=M\mathrm{SO}_r$, $s_r=\iota_r$ and $s_r^+=\iota_r^+$, and denote the structure maps by $\alpha_r$ and $\alpha_r^+$. These supplied spaces and structure maps are the two sequential Thom prespectra used here. Their stable homotopy groups are $\pi_n(M\mathrm O)=\operatorname{colim}_{r}\pi_{n+r}(M\mathrm O_r)$ and $\pi_n(M\mathrm{SO})=\operatorname{colim}_{r}\pi_{n+r}(M\mathrm{SO}_r)$, with transition maps given by suspension followed by the structure map. Only these two prespectra are used; no general Thom-spectrum theory is developed here. For each fixed n, the displayed colimit is taken over a tail r≥r₀ with r+n≥1, exactly as in [[def-stable-homotopy-groups-of-a-sequential-prespectrum]].
items.strategy: Use the fixed-coordinate embeddings iota_r(W)=R e_1⊕J(W). On each finite Stiefel stage the frame formula (v_1,…,v_r)↦(e_1,Jv_1,…,Jv_r) is continuous and equivariant for the block inclusion O(r)→O(r+1), so it descends through the Grassmannian quotient and its weak direct-limit topology. The fiber map (t,v)↦t e_1+Jv is an isometry ε¹⊕γ_r→iota_r^*γ_{r+1}; for the oriented bundles use the same construction with orientation e_1∧J_*o and the block inclusion SO(r)→SO(r+1). The local two-sheeted-cover lemma supplies the lifted BSO Schubert CW structure; rank zero is the point with its positive line. The disk/sphere quotient and trivial-line Thom identification give the based homeomorphism S¹∧Th(γ_r)≅Th(ε¹⊕γ_r), with the sphere coordinate first. Compose this homeomorphism, the displayed bundle isometry, and the Thom map of the actual pullback-bundle projection to Th(γ_{r+1}). That projection preserves the disk and sphere subspaces, so the quotient universal property makes the structure map based and continuous; the same argument applies to MSO. For the level topology, trivialize the pulled-back bundle over each Schubert characteristic disk. The disk/sphere quotient contributes one cell of dimension d+r over each d-cell, attached along the base boundary and fiber sphere. The finite-stage attaching quotients have their stated topology by the compact-to-Hausdorff quotient test. For the infinite disk bundle, every compact Hausdorff test map projects to a compact subset of the base and hence, by the cited compact-image result, lies over a finite Schubert subcomplex. It factors through the corresponding finite disk-bundle stage. The characteristic-disk tests therefore give the weak attachment topology; the quotient map test gives the same weak topology on the Thom space. The finite-boundary attachment lemma proves that this weak cell topology is Hausdorff and closure-finite. A subset is closed exactly when its inverse image in every compact characteristic ball is closed, so the compact-test characterization proves compact generation. Every compact Hausdorff test image is compact in this Hausdorff CW space and hence closed by the compact-subset theorem; this proves weak Hausdorffness. The basepoint is a CW vertex, and the relative-CW cofibration result makes its inclusion a cofibration. Thus every level is a well-pointed based CGWH CW space, as required by the sequential-prespectrum definition. Rank zero is separately S⁰. The stable-homotopy-group definition then supplies the stated colimits over admissible cofinal tails. These are explicit fixed maps, not maps identified only up to arbitrary classifying homotopy; no Omega-prespectrum condition or general represented-spectrum comparison is asserted. MO Thom normalization uses canonical F2 orientations; MSO uses its supplied ordered integral orientation or its coefficient image.

items.title: Admissible composites present the mod-two square algebra
items.statement: Assume AC. The natural map $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{Adem}}\to\mathcal A_{\mathrm{Sq}}$ is an isomorphism. In each degree $N$, its admissible composites $Sq^I$ with $|I|=N$ form an $\mathbb F_2$-basis. Thus the Adem relations impose all algebraic relations among composites of the published Steenrod squares.
items.strategy: Adem reduction spans the abstract quotient by admissible words. For a putative nonzero homogeneous relation of degree N among their natural operations, evaluate every term on the same product class on (RP^(N+1))^(N+1). The leading-monomial lemma applies to every sequence. Its largest occurring leading monomial cannot cancel against terms with smaller leading monomials, so the relation is nonzero. The identity is nonzero in degree zero. Since the quotient relations are homogeneous, degreewise independence makes the already surjective quotient-to-operation map injective.

items.title: A transgressive simple fiber system gives a polynomial base
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $F\to E\to B$ be a Serre fibration with $E$ contractible and $B$ simply connected CW. The hypotheses concern the actual strict fiber cohomology ring; no CW-type or homotopy-equivalence assertion for the fiber is assumed. Suppose $H^*(F;\mathbb F_2)$ has a basis consisting of the finite products of **distinct** positive-degree classes $x_\lambda$, including the empty product, and only finitely many $x_\lambda$ occur in each degree. Suppose classes $y_\lambda\in H^{|x_\lambda|+1}(B,*;\mathbb F_2)$ satisfy $\delta x_\lambda=p^*y_\lambda$. Then

$$\mathbb F_2[Y_\lambda]\xrightarrow{\cong}H^*(B;\mathbb F_2), \qquad Y_\lambda\longmapsto y_\lambda.$$

No assertion that $x_\lambda^2=0$ is required.
items.strategy: Build a model spectral sequence for each simple fiber generator with exterior x and polynomial Y, whose only differential is xY^a↦Y^(a+1) on page |x|+1. Tensor these factor sequences degreewise. Published vector-space bases and AC split complexes into homology plus contractible pairs; the tensor universal property, tensor/direct-sum and tensor-unit interfaces give the page-homology comparison, and H⊗id contracts each tensor pair. Positive degrees and local finiteness ensure only finitely many factors contribute per total degree. Evaluate squarefree fiber monomials and polynomial base monomials on the actual classes. Relative lifts and Leibniz give a morphism on every page; it is additive, not necessarily multiplicative in the fiber direction. The fiber axis and limiting scalar pages are isomorphic. Item 7d therefore identifies the base E_2 axis; there the map is the asserted polynomial ring homomorphism. Only computed strict-fiber cohomology is required.

items.title: Torsion Eilenberg–Mac Lane spaces are rationally acyclic
items.statement: Assume AC. If T is any torsion abelian group and n≥1, every CW K(T,n) has H_0(K(T,n);Q)=Q and H_j(K(T,n);Q)=0 for j>0. No cardinality or finite-type restriction is imposed.
items.strategy: For K(T,1), each finitely generated subgroup is finite. Sum lifts in its finite weak-join cover to construct τ with p_#τ=|F|id; the weakly contractible cover has zero positive rational homology. Every rational cellular cycle in B_wT has finite support in one finite-subgroup subcomplex and bounds there. For n≥2, weakly approximate the strict loop fiber by a marked CW K(T,n−1), transfer its rational homology by the weak-equivalence lemma, and apply the one-row homological Serre sequence of the contractible path fibration.

items.title: Unoriented Thom cohomology away from two and its strict endpoint
items.statement: Assume AC. Let R be a nonzero commutative unital ring with 2 invertible, r>0, MO(r)=Th(γ_r), and MSO(r)=Th(γ_r⁺). Then reduced H^i(MO(r);R)=H^{i−r}(BO(r);O_R(γ_r)). For odd r this is zero in every degree. For r=2m it is the shifted module u e R[p₁,…,p_m], with |u|=r, |e|=r and |p_i|=4i, interpreted through the oriented cover, not as a global unoriented R-Thom class. In particular reduced H^i(MO(r);R)=0 for i<2r, whereas reduced H^{2r}(MO(2m);R)=R. For MSO(r), reduced H^i(MSO(r);R)=H^{i−r}(BSO(r);R).
items.strategy: Apply the orientation-local-system clause of the relative Thom theorem and the relative-to-reduced quotient comparison. Identify the sign-local-system cohomology with anti-invariants of BSO(r) by the transfer/sign lemma. In odd rank all polynomial generators are invariant, so anti-invariants vanish because 2 is invertible. In even rank the anti-invariant part is eR[p₁,…,p_{m−1},e²]. Upstairs both the oriented Thom class and e change sign, so their product is invariant and explains the descended shifted module. Apply the oriented Thom isomorphism separately to MSO. Keep the even-rank degree-2r class explicit.

items.title: Finite products and comparison cones have homological finite type
items.statement: Assume AC. Let Y be a finite product of CW K(Z/2,q) models with q≥1, including the empty product *. Then every H_n(Y;Z) is finitely generated and H^*(Y;F)=F in degree zero only for every field F of characteristic different from two. For any continuous f:X→Z between arbitrary spaces, the integral chain cone has an exact sequence 0→coker(H_nX→H_nZ)→H_n(Cone(C_*(f;Z)))→ker(H_{n−1}X→H_{n−1}Z)→0. If H_nZ and H_{n−1}X are finitely generated, its middle group is finitely generated. In particular this holds in every degree for X=MO(r) or MSO(r) and Z=Y a finite product as above. The raw cone is nonnegative and degreewise free, without any finite-rank assertion or topological-cone identification.
items.strategy: Induct on the finite number of factors using integral Künneth. Each degree involves finitely many tensor and Tor products of finitely generated groups; finite cyclic/free decomposition and extensions give finite generation. Away-from-two field Künneth and field duality give the stated cohomology. Extract the displayed kernel/cokernel sequence from the algebraic cone long exact sequence. Its outer groups are finitely generated by quotient preservation and Noetherian submodules, and lifting finitely many quotient generators proves finite generation of the extension. Apply the Thom finite-generation theorem for the source. The cone’s degree-n group is C_n(Y;Z)⊕C_{n−1}(X;Z), a finite sum of free singular chain groups.

items.title: Degreewise mod-two cohomology of the universal real Thom prespectrum
items.statement:
Assume AC, inherited from the shared bundle and Thom construction. Use the real levels $T_r=\operatorname{Th}(\gamma_r)$ and first-coordinate structure maps $\alpha_r:S^1\wedge T_r\to T_{r+1}$ of the shared Thom prespectrum. For $q\in\mathbb Z$ put $A_r(q)=\widetilde H^{r+q}(T_r;\mathbb F_2)$ and define the backwards bonding map

$$\rho_r(q)=\sigma^{-1}\alpha_r^*:A_{r+1}(q)\longrightarrow A_r(q),$$

where $\sigma$ is reduced cohomology suspension with the sphere coordinate first. Define

$$\widehat H^q(TO;\mathbb F_2)=\{(x_r)_{r\ge0}\in\prod_{r\ge0}A_r(q):\rho_r(q)x_{r+1}=x_r\text{ for every }r\},\qquad \widehat H^*(TO;\mathbb F_2)=\bigoplus_{q\in\mathbb Z}\widehat H^q(TO;\mathbb F_2).$$

The conditions are linear, so this is a well-defined vector space with componentwise operations. It is an inverse-limit prespectrum invariant; identifying it with represented spectrum cohomology would require a separate comparison theorem.

The normalized Thom isomorphisms give $A_r(q)\cong H^q(BO(r);\mathbb F_2)$, with $u_r$ the normalized rank-$r$ Thom class. The bonding-map computation and eventual constancy are proved in [[lem-stable-thom-cohomology-is-degreewise-eventually-constant]]: all terms vanish for $q<0$, and for $q\ge0$ projection to any rank $r\ge q$ identifies the compatible tuples with the weight-$q$ polynomial Thom module. In particular, writing $U=(u_r)$,

$$\widehat H^*(TO;\mathbb F_2)\cong\mathbb F_2[w_1,w_2,\ldots]U,\qquad |w_i|=i,\quad |U|=0.$$

This is a graded vector-space and characteristic-polynomial-module identification, justified by that lemma. It gives no ring structure from reduced finite-level cup products. Each weight is finite-dimensional.
items.strategy: The shared prespectrum supplies the based continuous maps and the fixed order of the suspension coordinate. The CW and suspension-normalization proof within the moved shared combined prespectrum definition identifies suspension of each Thom-module class with the class of the bundle after adding the first trivial line; the two Thom isomorphisms and the natural relative/reduced quotient comparison make that suspension an isomorphism in every required degree. Pullback followed by its inverse therefore has exactly the stated domain and codomain and is linear. The compatibility equations define a linear subspace of the product, since each bonding map is linear; componentwise addition and scalar multiplication preserve them. The direct sum over $q$ imposes finite grading support rather than a completion. The following eventual-constancy lemma separately justifies the resulting invariant and its computation; no general inverse-limit theorem is used.

items.title: Universal real Thom spaces are (r−1)-connected
items.statement: Assume AC, inherited from the cited bundle, cohomology, or operation suppliers. For each r≥2, T_r=Th(γ_r over BO(r)) is a nonempty (r−1)-connected based CW complex.
items.strategy: The universal Thom-space CW structure has the collapsed sphere bundle as its basepoint vertex and one cell of dimension d+r over each d-cell of BO(r). Thus the relative pair (T_r,*) has no cells below dimension r. Apply the high-relative-cells lemma to obtain (r−1)-connectivity.

items.title: The universal mod-two class detects admissible composites in the strict range
items.statement:
Assume AC. For $q\ge1$ let $K_q=K(\mathbb F_2,q)$ be a based CW model with its normalized fundamental class $\iota_q$. For $0\le i<q$, the map

\[
 \eta_{q,i}:\mathcal A^i\longrightarrow
 \widetilde H^{q+i}(K_q;\mathbb F_2),\qquad
 a\longmapsto a(\iota_q)
\]

is injective. If $f:X\to K_q$ classifies $z\in\widetilde H^q(X;\mathbb F_2)$, then $f^*\eta_{q,i}(a)=a(z)$.
items.strategy: Representability supplies the normalized universal class and its based classifying maps; square naturality gives the evaluation identity. Expand a nonzero degree-i operation in the admissible basis and evaluate it on the degree-q product of degree-one generators on (RP^(i+1))^q. Since every excess is at most i<q, the common leading-term test is nonzero. A classifying map pulls the universal evaluation back to this test, so vanishing universally is impossible. This includes the identity and the q=1 strict range.

items.title: External evaluation detects tensor-square operations
items.statement: Assume AC. For every d,e≥0, let X_d=(RP^L)^(d+1), X_e=(RP^L)^(e+1), with L≥max(d,e)+1 and P_d=∏x_i, P_e=∏y_j. The map A^d⊗A^e→H*(X_d;F₂)⊗H*(X_e;F₂), a⊗b↦a(P_d)⊗b(P_e), is injective; under Künneth, external products jointly detect every homogeneous tensor of square operations.
items.strategy: The admissible leading-monomial lemma makes each evaluation A^d→H*(X_d) injective. Extend bases of the two images to bases of the target spaces and use the resulting left inverses to show their tensor product is injective. Künneth embeds this tensor test as external-product evaluation; distinct bidegrees stay separate.

items.title: Polynomial mod-two cohomology of Eilenberg–Mac Lane spaces
items.statement:
Assume AC. For $q\ge1$,

$$H^*(K_q;\mathbb F_2) \cong\mathbb F_2[Sq^I\iota_q\mid I\text{ admissible},\ e(I)<q],$$

including the empty sequence, with the indicated classes as actual polynomial generators of degree $q+|I|$.
items.strategy: Prove the excess identities by instability and the top-square formula. An admissible sequence of excess q is uniquely obtained by repeatedly prepending the current class degree to a tail of excess <q; its value is the corresponding binary power. Start from the polynomial K(F_2,1) computation. Assuming the polynomial result for K_q, binary exponents give a simple system of distinct-power generators indexed bijectively by admissible sequences of excess ≤q, finite in every degree. Use Item 6's actual path fibration and weak-equivalence ring comparison to transfer this system to its strict fiber. Item 7c gives the fundamental relative lift; connector compatibility and naturality give all composite lifts, and Item 7b gives their exact transgressions, including the fiber class in degree 2q and all higher powers. Apply Item 7e to obtain the polynomial base generators with excess <q+1, proving generation and independence simultaneously.

items.title: First rational Hurewicz after killing lower torsion homotopy
items.statement: Assume AC. Let Y be a simply connected space and n≥2. If π_j(Y) is torsion for 2≤j<n, then H_j(Y;Q)=0 for 0<j<n and actual Hurewicz induces an isomorphism π_n(Y)⊗Q→H_n(Y;Q). CW type is not required.
items.strategy: First replace Y by a based weak CW approximation. At each j<n use integral Hurewicz, the cohomological UCT, and representability to map the current (j−1)-connected CW space to K(π_j,j) by the identity in degree j. Its strict homotopy fiber is j-connected, preserves all higher homotopy, and is rational-homology equivalent to the previous space by the one-column Serre sequence over a torsion K-group. Weakly approximate that fiber and repeat finitely many times. Integral Hurewicz on the final (n−1)-connected CW space and naturality give the claimed map.

items.title: Finite-generation cohomological UCT gives integral cone comparison
items.statement: Assume AC. Let D≥0 and let C be a nonnegative free integral chain complex whose H_i(C) are finitely generated for 0≤i≤D. If H^i(Hom_Z(C,Q))=0 and H^i(Hom_Z(C,F_p))=0 for every prime p in those degrees, then H_i(C)=0 for 0≤i≤D. Consequently, for a continuous map f:X→Y with degreewise finitely generated integral homology, field cohomology isomorphisms f*:H^i(Y;F)→H^i(X;F) for F=Q and every F_p and 0≤i≤D imply integral homology isomorphisms f_* for i<D and surjectivity for i=D. No degree-D injectivity or degree-D+1 field hypothesis is asserted.
items.strategy: Cohomological UCT surjects each zero field cohomology group onto Hom(H_i(C),F). Finite abelian-group decomposition shows that Q detects any nonzero free summand and F_p detects any nonzero p-primary summand, so H_i(C)=0. For C=Cone(C_*(f;Z)), use the cone finite-generation lemma and dualize the degreewise split cone sequence. Its five-term cohomology segment has the adjacent maps f* in degrees i−1 and i; their isomorphisms force cone cohomology to vanish through D, including degree zero with negative terms zero. The integral cone exact sequence then gives isomorphisms strictly below D and a surjection at D. Injectivity at D would require cone homology vanishing at D+1 and is not inferred.

items.title: Stable universal Thom cohomology is eventually constant in every degree
items.statement: Assume AC through the published Thom and universal-bundle suppliers. For the preceding compatible-tuple invariant, the normalized Thom isomorphisms identify $\rho_r(q)$ with the homogeneous-weight-$q$ map $\mathbb F_2[w_1,\ldots,w_{r+1}]^q\to\mathbb F_2[w_1,\ldots,w_r]^q$ sending $w_i$ to $w_i$ for $i\le r$ and $w_{r+1}$ to zero. If $q<0$ all terms are zero. If $q\ge0$, every bonding map with $r\ge q$ is an isomorphism, and projection to any level $r\ge q$ identifies $\widehat H^q(TO;\mathbb F_2)$ with $\mathbb F_2[w_1,\ldots,w_r]^q u_r$. Writing $U=(u_r)$, this gives $\widehat H^*(TO;\mathbb F_2)\cong\mathbb F_2[w_1,w_2,\ldots]U$, with $|w_i|=i$ and $|U|=0$, as a graded vector space and as a module over the stable characteristic polynomial algebra. Each homogeneous piece is finite-dimensional. The assertion is a Thom-module computation, not an identification of reduced cup rings or a general spectrum-comparison theorem.
items.strategy: Let $\Phi_r(a)=a u_r$. The specified first-coordinate stabilization pulls back $\gamma_{r+1}$ to $\varepsilon^1\oplus\gamma_r$. Thom pullback naturality and the suspension normalization proved within that moved shared definition give $\alpha_r^*\Phi_{r+1}(a)=\sigma\Phi_r(s_r^*a)$, so $\Phi_r^{-1}\rho_r\Phi_{r+1}=s_r^*$. Stiefel–Whitney naturality, the Whitney formula, and trivial-line normalization identify $s_r^*w_i$ with $w_i$ below the old rank and with zero above it. Apply the published $BO(r)$ polynomial theorem. No weight-$q$ monomial contains a variable of weight exceeding $q$, so the map is bijective for $r\ge q$. A value at any such tail level extends uniquely to later levels by inverse bonding isomorphisms and to earlier levels by the original bonding maps; this gives the stated compatible-tuple computation without a general spectral comparison. The Thom-class normalization proves compatibility of $U$. Characteristic polynomials act componentwise after restriction to each rank, giving the claimed graded module. In weight $q$, only variables $w_i$ with $i\le q$ can appear, and each exponent is at most $q/i$, so there are finitely many monomials. Negative weights vanish by the Thom isomorphism. Rank zero and degree zero use $T_0=S^0$ and its normalized reduced Thom class.

items.title: The admissible square algebra is a connected bialgebra
items.statement: Assume AC. The mod-two algebra A generated by the Steenrod squares is a connected nonnegatively graded bialgebra. Its coproduct is the algebra homomorphism Δ(Sqⁿ)=Σ_{i+j=n}Sqⁱ⊗Sqʲ, with counit ε(Sq⁰)=1 and ε(Sqⁿ)=0 for n>0.
items.strategy: Define coproduct and counit on the free associative algebra. Coassociativity and the counit identities hold on generators. Cartan and tensor-evaluation faithfulness show each Adem generator maps into ker(q⊗q)=I⊗T+T⊗I. Multiplicativity and the fact that this kernel is a two-sided ideal extend the coideal condition to the full Adem ideal; positive-degree generators also force the counit to vanish on that ideal. Descend the maps to A and use the admissible basis for connectedness.

items.title: Metastable cohomology of mod-two Eilenberg–Mac Lane spaces
items.statement:
Assume AC. For $q\ge1$ and $0\le i<q$, evaluation on the normalized mod-two fundamental class is an isomorphism

\[
 \eta_{q,i}:\mathcal A^i\xrightarrow{\cong}
 \widetilde H^{q+i}(K(\mathbb F_2,q);\mathbb F_2),\qquad
 a\longmapsto a(\iota_q).
\]

For a based classifying map $f$ of $z$, it satisfies $f^*\eta_{q,i}(a)=a(z)$. No integral identification and no degree-$2q$ endpoint claim is included.
items.strategy: The square algebra has the admissible basis by Item 4, independently of the EM computation. The polynomial presentation of Item 7 has generators of degrees at least q, so products of two positive generators cannot occur in degree q+i<2q. Its basis in that degree is exactly the single generators Sq^I iota_q with |I|=i; all admissible sequences of that degree have excess ≤i<q. Evaluation therefore takes the admissible operation basis bijectively to this cohomology basis. Item 5 also gives independent injectivity. Natural squares and the existing universal-operation corollary give the classifying-map formula. Include q=1,i=0 and make no degree-2q or integral identification.

items.title: Finite-range rational homology vanishing implies rational homotopy vanishing
items.statement: Assume AC. If Y is simply connected and H_j(Y;Q)=0 for 0<j≤D, then π_j(Y)⊗Q=0 for 2≤j≤D.
items.strategy: Induct on j using the first rational Hurewicz lemma: previously vanishing rational homotopy groups are torsion, so degree-j Hurewicz identifies the next rational homotopy group with zero homology. This is finite induction for each D.

items.title: Rational homotopy comparison with one endpoint surjection implies homology comparison
items.statement: Assume AC. Let f:W→X be a based map of 2-connected CW complexes and let D≥2. If π_i(f)⊗Q is an isomorphism for 2≤i≤D and a surjection for i=D+1, then H_i(f;Q) is an isomorphism for 0≤i≤D.
items.strategy: The strict homotopy fiber is simply connected. Exact rationalization of its homotopy sequence makes π_j(F)⊗Q vanish for 2≤j≤D, using the extra endpoint surjection when j=D. First rational Hurewicz then makes its homology vanish through D. The homological Serre sequence has only its bottom row in the relevant total degrees; its actual projection edge is an isomorphism through D. Compose with the mapping-path equivalence of W to identify this map with H_i(f;Q).

items.title: Stable Steenrod squares on universal Thom cohomology
items.statement: Assume AC, inherited from the cited bundle, cohomology, or operation suppliers. For $i\ge0$ and $x=(x_r)\in\widehat H^q(TO;\mathbb F_2)$, define $Sq^i x$ by the components $(Sq^i x)_r=Sq^i(x_r)$ in $\widetilde H^{r+q+i}(T_r;\mathbb F_2)$. At a negative finite-level source degree use the unique map from the zero cohomology group. These components form a compatible tuple, giving a linear map $Sq^i:\widehat H^q\to\widehat H^{q+i}$. They satisfy $Sq^0=\mathrm{id}$ and the published Adem relations, so their finite linear combinations and composites give an action of the mod-two square algebra on the graded invariant. For the stable normalized Thom vector $U$, $Sq^iU=w_iU$ with $w_0=1$; its rank-$r$ component is zero for $i>r$. The degree-zero stable vector $U$ is not subject to the instability bound for a degree-zero class of a space: its rank-$r$ representative has degree $r$. No freeness or homotopy-detection conclusion is asserted here.
items.strategy: Pullback naturality commutes each square with $\alpha_r^*$, and the published reduced suspension identity commutes it with $\sigma$ and $\sigma^{-1}$. Thus $\rho_r(q+i)Sq^i=Sq^i\rho_r(q)$, proving compatibility and linearity. Normalization and Adem identities hold at every finite level, hence on the tuples and their graded direct sum. The Thom identity gives $Sq^i u_r=w_i(\gamma_r)u_r$, including rank zero and the vanishing for $i>r$. Under the preceding eventual-constancy/polynomial-module identification these are exactly the components of $w_iU$. All stable-degree claims are checked through the actual level degrees $r+q$; no finite-level instability rule is incorrectly imposed at stable degree $q$.

items.title: Whitney-sum coalgebra on stable unoriented Thom cohomology
items.statement:
Assume AC, inherited from the cited bundle, cohomology, or operation suppliers. Let $\mathcal P=\mathbb F_2[w_1,w_2,\ldots]$ with $|w_k|=k$, and use the graded identification $M=\mathcal P U$ with $|U|=0$ and $w_0=1$. Extend $\Delta_P(w_k)=\sum_{i+j=k}w_i\otimes w_j$ uniquely to a unital algebra homomorphism $\Delta_P:\mathcal P\to\mathcal P\otimes\mathcal P$. Define the candidate maps $\Delta_M(fU)=\Delta_P(f)(U\otimes U)$, $\epsilon_M(fU)=f(0)$, and $\eta(1)=U$. These formulas specify the proposed Whitney-sum operations; their well-definedness, inverse-limit compatibility, and coalgebra axioms are proved in [[lem-whitney-sum-coalgebra-is-well-defined-on-stable-thom-cohomology]].


Each polynomial has finite support and each generator coproduct is a finite sum, so these are degree-preserving linear maps on $M$ and the ordinary graded tensor product. The rankwise geometric interpretation is the Thom pullback of an external Whitney sum, with

$$w_kU\longmapsto\sum_{i+j=k}(w_iU)\otimes(w_jU),\qquad U\longmapsto U\otimes U.$$

The cited well-definedness lemma proves agreement with that geometric pullback, stabilization compatibility, coassociativity, and both counit identities; these are obligations of the construction rather than additional premises.
items.strategy: This item fixes the polynomial formulas and the coaugmentation. The following local lemma constructs the rankwise Whitney-sum pullbacks, verifies their compatibility with both fixed-coordinate bonding systems using the external Thom product and relative field Künneth, and proves the counit and coassociativity identities. No represented-spectrum cohomology comparison is used.

items.title: Rational sphere homotopy below the first unstable degree
items.statement: Assume AC. For m≥2 and 1≤i≤2m−2, π_i(S^m)⊗Q is Q if i=m and zero otherwise. Hurewicz after tensoring with Q is an isomorphism in all these degrees; in degree m its integral version is the standard orientation-generator isomorphism; no finiteness of the torsion groups is asserted.
items.strategy: Map S^m to K(Z,m) by its orientation cohomology class. The strict homotopy fiber is m-connected. Its homological Serre sequence, using local K(Z,m) cohomology and field duality, inductively forces positive rational fiber homology to vanish through 2m−2: all incoming sources for column-zero terms vanish. Apply finite-range rational vanishing to the fiber and its homotopy exact sequence to transfer vanishing to the sphere. Integral Hurewicz supplies degree m.

items.title: The zero section proves injectivity of the Thom unit orbit
items.statement: Assume AC. For the stable Thom class U∈M⁰, the map ν:A→M, a↦aU, is injective in every degree.
items.strategy: For nonzero homogeneous a∈Aᵈ choose r=d+1 and X=(RPᴸ)^r with ᴸ≥d+1. The leading-monomial test gives a(P)≠0 for P=x₁⋯x_r. The zero section of the sum of the r tautological lines pulls its mod-two Thom class back to e₂(E)=w_r(E)=P. Naturality then makes the rank-r component of aU nonzero; distinct degrees cannot cancel.

items.title: Whitney sum defines the connected coalgebra on stable Thom cohomology
items.statement: Assume AC, inherited from the cited bundle, cohomology, or operation suppliers. Assume the displayed identification M=F₂[w₁,w₂,…]U and the formulas of [[def-whitney-sum-coalgebra-on-stable-unoriented-thom-cohomology]]. Then Δ_M:M→M⊗M is a degree-preserving coassociative coproduct, ε_M is a counit, and η(1)=U is a coaugmentation. M is connected and nonnegatively graded. For each p,q, the rankwise Thom pullback induced by γ_p⊕γ_q agrees with Δ_M under the Thom isomorphisms, commutes with the fixed-coordinate stabilization in each factor, and therefore induces the stated map on the degreewise inverse-limit invariant.
items.strategy: For each p,q, classify the external sum of the two universal bundles over BO(p)×BO(q). The Whitney formula gives the pullback of each w_k, and the external Thom-class formula gives U↦U⊗U. Each finite-rank Grassmannian has finitely many Schubert cells in each dimension; its Thom space therefore has finite-dimensional relative homology in every degree over F₂. This verifies the finite-free hypothesis of the cited relative Künneth lemma for the based Thom pairs (T_p,*),(T_q,*), identifying the target with the finite direct sum over degree splittings. Adjoining the specified first coordinate in either factor compares the two rankwise composites by the canonical coordinate permutation; naturality and mod-two Thom normalization preserve the formulas. Hence the maps commute with both bonding systems and induce the stated graded map on the degreewise inverse-limit invariant. On the polynomial generators both iterated coproducts send w_k to the sum over i+j+ℓ=k, while Δ_M(U)=U⊗U, so coassociativity extends multiplicatively. Evaluation at w_i=0 gives both counit identities; ε_M(U)=1 verifies the coaugmentation identities. Finally M⁰=F₂U and M has no negative degrees by the eventual-constancy lemma, proving connectedness and nonnegative grading.

items.title: Rational Hurewicz for arbitrary wedges of high-dimensional spheres
items.statement: Assume AC. Let W be the CW wedge of any set of spheres of dimensions at least c≥2. For 1≤i≤2c−2, π_i(W)⊗Q and H_i(W;Q) are the direct sum of Q indexed by spheres of dimension i, and actual Hurewicz identifies their orientation generators.
items.strategy: For a finite wedge embed it as the one-factor subcomplex of the finite product of its spheres. Every relative product cell has dimension at least 2c, so high-cell invariance identifies the required homotopy groups with the product groups; apply the sphere calculation. Cellular homology gives the same sphere generators. Compact cell support places every representative and homotopy for an arbitrary wedge in a finite subwedge, giving the filtered-colimit/direct-sum description. Rationalization and naturality preserve the actual Hurewicz map.

items.title: Stable Thom cohomology is a square-module coalgebra
items.statement: Assume AC. For a∈A and m∈M, the stable Steenrod action and Whitney-sum coproduct satisfy Δ_M(a·m)=Δ_A(a)·Δ_M(m), where A acts diagonally on M⊗M. The counit is compatible with the action, so M is an A-module coalgebra.
items.strategy: At finite ranks, naturality identifies the coproduct of Sqᵏm with Sqᵏ applied to the Whitney pullback. Cartan expands this as Σ_{i+j=k}(Sqⁱ⊗Sqʲ)Δ_M(m), exactly the diagonal action from Δ_A. Multiplicativity extends generator compatibility to all operations; grading gives counit compatibility.

items.title: Rational Hurewicz for highly connected CW complexes
items.statement: Assume AC. If a based CW complex X is (c−1)-connected with c≥2, the natural actual rationalized Hurewicz map π_i(X)⊗_Z Q→H_i(X;Q) is an isomorphism for c≤i≤2c−2. Lower positive rational homology vanishes. No finite-type, countability or finite-CW hypothesis is imposed, and no injectivity at 2c−1 is claimed.
items.strategy: For c=2 use integral first Hurewicz. For c≥3 put D=2c−2 and choose representatives of numerator-rescaled rational bases of π_j(X)⊗Q for c≤j≤D+1. Their CW wedge W maps continuously to X. Wedge Hurewicz gives rational homotopy isomorphisms through D, and the chosen endpoint spheres give surjectivity at D+1. The finite-range comparison gives homology isomorphisms through D. The Hurewicz naturality square then proves the desired map is an isomorphism. Basepoint transport extends the vertex-based construction to the prescribed basepoint.

items.title: Stable unoriented Thom cohomology is free over the square algebra
items.statement: Assume AC. Under the Steenrod action, M is a free graded left A-module. With Q=M/A⁺M, the freeness isomorphism is M≅A⊗Q; any homogeneous basis of Q lifts to a free A-basis of M.
items.strategy: The preceding items provide a connected graded bialgebra A, a connected graded module coalgebra M, and injectivity of a↦aU. Apply the locally proved connected module-coalgebra freeness theorem. Stable degreewise finite dimensionality supplies finite-dimensional generator pieces for the detector construction, not an extra hypothesis of the freeness theorem.
