items.title: Finite Thom classifying detector map
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $\mathcal A$ be the mod-two square algebra acting on $M=\widehat H^*(TO;\mathbb F_2)$, let $\mathcal A^+=\bigoplus_{j>0}\mathcal A^j$ be its positive-degree ideal, and put $Q=M/\mathcal A^+M$ as in the freeness theorem. Fix once and for all a homogeneous basis $B=\coprod_{d\ge0}B_d$ of $Q$ and a degree-preserving section $s:Q\to M$ of the quotient map, using AC; these choices are shared by every rank. For $b\in B_d$ set $m_b=s(b)$ and $d_b=d$. For each $r\ge2$, set $B(r)=\bigcup_{0\le d<r}B_d$. The freeness theorem makes all $m_b$, for $b\in B$, a homogeneous free $\mathcal A$-basis of $M$. Via the eventual-constancy isomorphism $M^d\cong\widetilde H^{r+d}(T_r;\mathbb F_2)$, let $\bar m_{b,r}$ be the rank-r coordinate of the same fixed $m_b$, and choose a based representative $f_{r,b}:T_r\to K(\mathbb F_2,r+d_b)$ of its representing class. Set $P_r=\prod_{b\in B(r)}K(\mathbb F_2,r+d_b)$ and define the candidate based detector $f_r:T_r\to P_r$ by its coordinate maps. The same basis and lifts are used at every rank, so the coordinates are compatible with prespectrum stabilization. The finite existence and continuity argument is recorded in [[lem-finite-thom-classifying-detector-map-exists-and-is-continuous]].
items.strategy: Use AC once to fix a single homogeneous basis B=⊔_{d≥0}B_d of Q and a degree-preserving section s:Q→M. Reuse the same lifts m_b=s(b) at every rank, and for rank r use only the finite initial segment B(r)=⋃_{d<r}B_d. The freeness theorem makes all lifts a free A-basis; finite-dimensional degree pieces make B(r) finite. Eventual constancy supplies the rank-r classes, Eilenberg–Mac Lane representability supplies based coordinate maps, and the finite-product universal property assembles f_r. This global choice is the one used in the suspension-compatibility lemma.

references.title: Tom Weston, An Introduction to Cobordism Theory
references.locator: §13, printed pp. 24–25: classifying maps to Eilenberg–Mac Lane spaces and the strict comparison range; the finite generator product is constructed locally.

items.title: The finite Thom classifying detector map exists and is continuous
items.statement: Assume AC and the construction of [[def-finite-thom-classifying-detector-map]], using the single global basis B=⋃_{d≥0}B_d and section fixed there. For every r≥2, the initial segment B(r)=⋃_{0≤d<r}B_d is finite; for each b∈B_d with d_b=d, the coordinate class m̄_{b,r}∈H̃^{r+d_b}(T_r;F₂) has a based representative f_{r,b}:T_r→K(F₂,r+d_b) representing that class; and the coordinate family uniquely defines a continuous based map f_r:T_r→P_r.
items.strategy: For each d<r, M^d is finite-dimensional by the degreewise stabilization calculation, so its quotient Q^d is finite-dimensional. The global homogeneous basis and section were fixed once in the definition; their lifts form a free A-basis of M by the connected module-coalgebra freeness theorem, and the same low-degree generators are reused at every rank. There are only r selected degrees, each with a finite basis, so B(r) is finite. Since r>d, eventual constancy identifies each fixed m_b with an actual reduced cohomology class of T_r. Eilenberg–Mac Lane representability gives a based homotopy class representing it; choose an actual based representative for each of the finitely many coordinates. The finite product universal property gives the unique continuous based map f_r with these projections. The single global choice also gives the stated suspension compatibility.

references.title: Tom Weston, An Introduction to Cobordism Theory
references.locator: §13, printed pp. 24–25: classifying maps to Eilenberg–Mac Lane spaces; the finite generator product and its continuity are verified locally.

items.title: The finite Thom detector is a mod-two cohomology isomorphism below 2r
items.statement: Assume AC. For the detector f_r:T_r→P_r, the pullback f_r*:H̃ᵏ(P_r;F₂)→H̃ᵏ(T_r;F₂) is an isomorphism for every k<2r. No comparison is asserted at k=2r.
items.strategy: Below r both reduced groups vanish by Thom-cell connectivity and the connectivity of every factor. For r≤k<2r, write e=k−r; stable Thom cohomology is the direct sum of A^{e−d_b} over generator degrees d_b≤e. The strict Eilenberg–Mac Lane theorem identifies each factor contribution with that operation space. Products of positive-degree factor classes first occur in degree 2r, so below the endpoint the product cohomology is the direct sum of single-factor contributions; f_r* maps these bases identically.

references.title: Tom Weston, An Introduction to Cobordism Theory
references.locator: §13, Theorem 13.2, printed pp. 24–25; the strict <2r endpoint and finite product decomposition are proved locally.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology
references.locator: §1.3, Theorems 1.32 and 1.36 and comparison proof, printed pp. 52–58.

items.title: The finite Thom detector is an integral homology isomorphism below 2r−1
items.statement: Assume AC. For f_r:T_r→P_r, f_{r*}:H_i(T_r;Z)→H_i(P_r;Z) is an isomorphism for i<2r−1 and a surjection for i=2r−1. No endpoint injectivity is asserted.
items.strategy: Put D=2r−1 and use the mod-two comparison through D, together with odd-primary and rational cohomology vanishing in the strict range, to obtain cohomology isomorphisms over Q and every F_p through D. Finite generation of both homology groups gives a finitely generated integral cone. The cohomological UCT maps its zero field-cohomology groups onto Hom(H_i(C_f),F); Q detects free summands and each F_p detects p-torsion. Thus cone homology vanishes through D, yielding the stated iso/surjection endpoint.

references.title: Tom Weston, An Introduction to Cobordism Theory
references.locator: §13, Theorem 13.2, printed pp. 24–25; coefficient and integral-cone upgrades and the strict endpoint are proved locally.

references.title: John Milnor and James Stasheff, Characteristic Classes
references.locator: Chapter 18, §§18.1–18.4: universal Thom spaces and Thom cohomology.

items.title: The finite Thom detector is a homotopy isomorphism through 2r−2
items.statement: Assume AC. For r≥2, f_r induces π_i(T_r)≅π_i(P_r) for 1≤i≤2r−2. On π_{r+n}, for 0≤n≤r−2, the target is F₂^{B_n} and its coordinates are evaluation on the chosen stable Thom classes.
items.strategy: T_r and P_r are path-connected and simply connected. Replace the arbitrary product target by the finite-range draft's relative CW approximation, then apply its mapping-cylinder/relative-Hurewicz comparison with N=2r−1, using the integral iso below N and surjection at N. Coordinatewise homotopy groups of the finite product of Eilenberg–Mac Lane spaces identify the detector coordinates; the cutoff r≥n+2 is exactly the strict Hurewicz range.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
references.locator: Theorem 4.32 and Corollary 4.33, printed pp. 366–368: relative Hurewicz and finite-range comparison method.

items.title: Stable Thom detector coordinates commute with suspension
items.statement: Assume AC. Fix n≥0 and V_n=F₂^{B_n}. For every r≥n+2 let D_{r,n}:π_{r+n}(T_r)→V_n pair a sphere class with the rank-r stable-coordinate classes m_{r,b}, b∈B_n. If β_r:S¹∧T_r→T_{r+1} is the prespectrum structure map, then D_{r+1,n}∘(β_r)_*=D_{r,n} under suspension of representatives.
items.strategy: The inverse-limit coordinate identity says σ⁻¹β_r*m_{r+1,b}=m_{r,b}. Naturality of the Kronecker pairing and the cross-product formula for the mod-two fundamental class of S¹∧S^{r+n} show that every evaluation coordinate is unchanged by stabilization. The same map is the Eilenberg–Mac Lane coordinate of the finite detector.

references.title: Daniel S. Freed, Bordism: Old and New
references.locator: Lectures 7–10, printed pp. 55–91: Thom classes, Thom spectra, and stabilization; the coordinate-pairing compatibility is proved locally.

items.title: Stable unoriented Thom homotopy is injectively detected
items.statement: Assume AC. For each n≥0, the stable group π_n(MO)=colim_r π_{r+n}(T_r) maps injectively to V_n=F₂^{B_n} by the compatible detector coordinates D_{r,n}, using the cofinal tail r≥n+2.
items.strategy: The finite-range theorem makes every D_{r,n} an isomorphism on that tail, and the previous lemma makes the diagram commute with prespectrum stabilization. If a stable class has zero detector, every later representative has zero detector and hence vanishes at that rank; the cofinal-tail description of the colimit proves the original class is zero. No stabilization isomorphism is assumed in advance.

references.title: Daniel S. Freed, Bordism: Old and New
references.locator: Lectures 10–12, printed pp. 86–105: Thom spectra, stable homotopy, and the rational Hurewicz application; the cofinal-tail injection is proved locally.

title: Thom Spectra and Unoriented Bordism Detection — Examples

items.title: Low-degree admissible Steenrod monomials
items.statement: Assume AC. The admissible bases in degrees 0–4 are respectively {1}, {Sq¹}, {Sq²}, {Sq³,Sq²Sq¹}, and {Sq⁴,Sq³Sq¹}. The Adem relations give Sq¹Sq¹=0, Sq¹Sq²=Sq³, and Sq²Sq²=Sq³Sq¹.
items.strategy: Enumerate positive sequences of each total degree, retain those satisfying i_j≥2i_{j+1}, and use the Adem reduction theorem for spanning and the admissible-basis theorem for independence. Substitute the three displayed pairs into the Adem relation.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
references.locator: §4.L, printed p. 499: Adem reduction to admissible monomials.

items.title: A strict metastable Eilenberg–Mac Lane range
items.statement: Assume AC. For K=K(F₂,3), H³(K;F₂)=F₂{ι₃}, H⁴(K;F₂)=F₂{Sq¹ι₃}, and H⁵(K;F₂)=F₂{Sq²ι₃}. The strict operation range has i<3; at degree 6 the polynomial presentation also has ι₃², so the endpoint is excluded.
items.strategy: Apply the strict metastable theorem to identify cohomology with A^i for i=0,1,2, and use the admissible basis to list these spaces. The full polynomial theorem explains the degree-six endpoint, which is not included in the strict-range claim.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology
references.locator: §1.3, polynomial cohomology of K(F₂,q) and the comparison theorem, printed pp. 52–58.

references.title: Tom Weston, An Introduction to Cobordism Theory
references.locator: §8, printed p. 15: universal Steenrod operations on Eilenberg–Mac Lane spaces.

items.title: A Steenrod operation on the universal Thom class
items.statement: Assume AC, inherited from the cited bundle, cohomology, or operation suppliers. In stable mod-two Thom cohomology, Sq³(U)=w₃U. At rank 3, Sq³(u₃)=w₃(γ₃)u₃; at rank 2 the component is zero because w₃(γ₂)=0 and Sq³(u₂)=0 by instability.
items.strategy: Use the stable-square identity Sqⁱ(U)=wᵢU componentwise. Truncate the third Stiefel–Whitney class at rank two and apply instability to the degree-two Thom class; at rank three the identity agrees with the top-square formula.

references.title: John Milnor and James Stasheff, Characteristic Classes
references.locator: Chapter 16: the Thom identity relating Steenrod squares of the Thom class to Stiefel–Whitney classes.

items.title: The rational Hurewicz range for the four-sphere
items.statement: Assume AC. For S⁴, the rational Hurewicz map is an isomorphism in degrees 4, 5, and 6: π₄(S⁴)⊗Q≅H₄(S⁴;Q)≅Q, and both π_i(S⁴)⊗Q and H_i(S⁴;Q) vanish for i=5,6.
items.strategy: Use the one-cell compression supplier on the standard CW pair (S⁴,*): every based cube Iʲ→S⁴ with j=1,2,3 deforms rel boundary into the 0-cell, so S⁴ is 3-connected. Sphere homology with coefficient group Q computes the target groups. Apply the locally proved rational Hurewicz theorem with c=4 and the rational sphere calculation through degree 6.

references.title: Daniel S. Freed, Bordism: Old and New
references.locator: Lecture 12, printed p. 105, where rational Hurewicz is invoked; the stated range and sphere example are proved using the local A-page theorem.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
references.locator: Theorem 4.32 and Corollary 4.33, printed pp. 366–368: the integral relative-Hurewicz comparison used in the local range proof.
